extracted.intended_audience: institutional press officers, science communicators, and science journalists (UK context)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting science press releases to maximize accurate media pickup and to mitigate 'churnalism' in UK science journalism; balances wire-friendly reach with specialist-targeted material for deeper coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-outlet detection-resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases that yield differentiated stories at different outlets are higher-quality (genuine news) than releases that yield identical stories everywhere (pure churnalism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers can encourage differentiated coverage by supplying outlet-specific quotes and angles so that stories are not near-identical across outlets; detection-resistance indicates the release contains substantive, negotiable news value rather than a one-size-fits-all wire item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialist-correspondent targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases pitched to remaining specialist science correspondents (with appropriate scientific depth, methodological detail, and prior-literature context) earn deeper coverage than wire-blast releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sufficient scientific depth, methodological detail and context to make it worth a specialist's time; personalise or route material toward the fewer surviving specialist reporters rather than only blasting generic copy to general news desks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-homogenization measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers concerned with churnalism should offer different angles to different outlets (exclusives, region-specific framings, embargoed first looks) to avoid homogenous reprinting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately trade uniform, maximal reach for diversified coverage by offering exclusives, tailoring regional framings, or providing differentiated story hooks per outlet to reduce identical replication across the media landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release-as-final-product disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases should indicate that no journalist has independently verified the work, so editors can decide whether to invest the verification cost or run as-is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about the verification status of the findings; explicit disclosure allows editors to judge whether to run the item without further checking or to allocate resources for independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent-verification path
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases should make independent verification cheap (links to data, named external experts, study protocol) — addressing churnalism's root cause (verification cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct links to datasets, study protocols, code, and contact details for independent experts; lowering the time and effort required for verification increases the likelihood of accurate, substantiated reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-press-release supply
rubrics_metrics.description: On contested topics, releases should anticipate counter-releases from competing groups and supply enough context for the journalist to triangulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include caveats, comparative context, and references to alternative viewpoints or competing claims so journalists can place findings in a broader debate rather than reproducing one-sided claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo with prep window
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes that give specialists time to call independent experts before lift produce higher-quality coverage than zero-prep-window blasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoes that allow adequate lead time for specialists to consult external experts and check materials; avoid immediate-release blasts that leave no time for independent scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-database posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting the press release to a public database (EurekAlert, AlphaGalileo) plus the issuing institution's news site supports both pickup and after-the-fact accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute via recognized public channels as well as institutional pages to aid discoverability, create an auditable record, and facilitate both broad pickup and later accountability or correction if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness trade-off and bifurcated strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A release optimized for churnalism will be picked up most widely (homogeneously) but will have low long-run trust capital; a release optimized for quality coverage will be picked up by fewer outlets but earn deeper, more accurate, more durable stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a bifurcated approach where appropriate: produce a wire-friendly base release for broad reach plus supplementary, deeper specialist material (methods, data, expert contacts, tailored angles) to support high-quality specialist coverage.
